summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with a history of cholangiocarcinoma and recurrent biliary stent infections, was admitted with fever and chills concerning for cholangitis. He underwent an urgent ERCP, which was complicated by acute hemorrhage from a likely portobiliary fistula, resulting in a hemoglobin drop from 11.3 to 7.5 g/dL. He was stabilized with IV fluids and one unit of packed red blood cells, then transferred to the ICU. A portal vein stent was successfully placed to seal the fistula. Blood cultures grew ESBL-producing E. coli, sensitive to meropenem, and he was treated with IV antibiotics, later transitioned to ertapenem. His infection resolved, and he was discharged home with plans to complete a 14-day antibiotic course and restart suppressive therapy with delafloxacin and fosfomycin. Follow-up was arranged with oncology and primary care.
